set.title: Search and rescue starter set
set.description: Four search and rescue procedures written by Resgrid as a starting point: missing person intake, search urgency, initial response for a lost person, and team check-in and check-out. Adapt them to your team's training, your area and the agency that holds search authority.

protocols.name: Missing person intake
protocols.description: What to ask the reporting party and record before teams are sent.

items.html: Name, age, sex, height, build and a recent photograph if one is available.
Clothing, footwear (with sole pattern if known), equipment and colours.
Medical conditions, medicines needed, and any cognitive or mental health concerns.
Experience in the outdoors and the area; known habits when lost.
Where and when the person was last seen or last known to be, and by whom.
Intended route and destination, and the vehicle and where it is parked.
Mobile phone number and carrier, and when the phone was last used.

blocks.title: Personal information
blocks.html: Share the subject's medical and personal details only with the people working the search.

protocols.name: Search urgency assessment
protocols.description: A quick way to decide how urgent the response is, from the subject, the weather, the terrain and time.

blocks.html: Score each factor from 1 (most urgent) to 3 (least urgent) and add them up. A lower total means a faster, larger response. Use your team's own scale if it has one.

blocks.title: Always urgent
blocks.html: A missing child, a person at risk of self-harm and a person with dementia are urgent whatever the total.

protocols.name: Initial response to a lost person
protocols.description: The first hours: hasty search of likely spots, containment of the search area and setting up command.

items.html: Set up command at or near the point last seen, out of the search area, and start a log.
Protect the point last seen and any tracks or scent articles from being disturbed.
Send hasty teams to the most likely places: trails, drainages, decision points, water and shelters.
Contain the area: post people at trailheads, road crossings and other exits, and light or mark attraction points.
Request more resources early if the urgency is high; it is easier to stand teams down than to call them in late.

blocks.title: Team safety
blocks.html: No team searches alone or without communications, and every team checks in and out with command.

protocols.name: Team check-in and check-out
protocols.description: Accountability for every searcher: check-in, briefing, assignment, debriefing and check-out.

items.html: Record each searcher's name, team, qualifications, contact number and expected time out.
Check equipment and communications before the team leaves.
Give the subject's description, the assignment area, the search method, hazards, radio channels and the check-in times.
Debrief every team: area covered, how well it was searched, clues found, hazards met.
Check each searcher out by name; nobody leaves without checking out.
